prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1342; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, insured vehicle struck from behind by a sedan. Claimant reports neck stiffness and pain in the left wrist. No police report filed at scene; the other driver exchanged information only. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured.

Entry 2: Contacted the claimant to introduce myself and explain the claims process. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and said she would handle the matter herself. Confirmed she received the medical authorization form and the rental car coverage details. She reports she was seen at urgent care and X-rays showed a fracture of the wrist, now in a splint. Advised her to keep all medical bills and receipts.

Entry 3: Received the urgent care records. Diagnosis is a fracture of the distal radius of the left wrist, with a referral to an orthopedic specialist. Claimant is scheduled for a follow-up consult next week. Noted that the claimant may need time off work; asked her to send documentation from her employer once available. Reviewed the at-fault determination: the other driver's vehicle rear-ended the insured, and the rear driver's liability appears clear.

Entry 4: Spoke with the at-fault driver's carrier to confirm liability acceptance and policy limits. Their adjuster acknowledged the rear-end impact but disputed the extent of the claimant's injury, citing a pre-existing wrist complaint. Requested prior medical records from the claimant to address the dispute. Claimant said she has no prior wrist problems and will provide her primary care records.

Entry 5: Received the orthopedic consult notes confirming the wrist fracture and recommending a cast for six weeks followed by physical therapy. Claimant returned the signed medical authorization and a copy of her employer's leave letter. Set up a reserve review for bodily injury and property damage. Will follow up with the other carrier regarding their response to the pre-existing condition question.
